whatIsQLearning.title: What is Q-Learning?
whatIsQLearning.description: Q-Learning is a value-based reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the optimal action to take in each state by maintaining a Q-table:
whatIsQLearning.qTable: Q-Table: Maps state-action pairs to expected rewards (Q-values)
whatIsQLearning.bellman: Bellman Equation: Q(s,a) = Q(s,a) + α[r + γ·max(Q(s',a')) - Q(s,a)]
whatIsQLearning.alpha: α (Alpha): Learning rate (difficulty-adjusted) - how much new info overrides old
whatIsQLearning.gamma: γ (Gamma): Discount factor (0.95) - importance of future rewards
whatIsQLearning.epsilon: ε (Epsilon): Exploration rate (starts at 1.0, decays based on difficulty)

explorationVsExploitation.title: Exploration vs Exploitation
explorationVsExploitation.description: The agent uses an epsilon-greedy strategy to balance learning and performance:
explorationVsExploitation.exploration: Exploration (ε = 1.0 → 0.01): Take random actions to discover new paths
explorationVsExploitation.exploitation: Exploitation (1 - ε): Use learned Q-values to take best known action
explorationVsExploitation.decay: Epsilon Decay: Gradually shift from exploration to exploitation as agent learns
explorationVsExploitation.note: Watch the Epsilon (ε) metric decrease over time - as it approaches 0.01, the agent transitions from random exploration to exploiting learned strategies!

rewardStructure.title: Reward Structure
rewardStructure.description: The agent receives rewards for its actions:
rewardStructure.normalMove: Normal Move: -0.5 base penalty + directional bonus
rewardStructure.closer: Move closer to goal: +0.1 (reward shaping guides learning)
rewardStructure.away: Move away from goal: -0.1 (discourages wrong direction)
rewardStructure.episodeLimit: Episode Limit: 1000 steps max to prevent infinite loops
rewardStructure.shaping: The reward shaping (directional bonus) acts like a compass, guiding the agent toward the goal while still discovering the optimal path through Q-learning!

howQLearningLearns.title: How Q-Learning Learns
howQLearningLearns.step1: Initialize: Start with empty Q-table (all values = 0)
howQLearningLearns.step2: Episode Loop: Agent spawns at green position
howQLearningLearns.step3: Choose Action: ε-greedy (explore random or exploit best Q-value)
howQLearningLearns.step4: Execute: Move agent, observe reward and next state
howQLearningLearns.step5: Update Q-Value: Apply Bellman equation to learn from experience
howQLearningLearns.step6: Repeat: Until reaching red goal or step limit (agents blink rapidly between cells)
howQLearningLearns.step7: Decay ε: Reduce exploration rate based on maze difficulty
howQLearningLearns.step8: Next Episode: Reset agent, repeat with updated Q-values
howQLearningLearns.insight: Over time, Q-values propagate backward from the goal, creating a "gradient" that guides the agent! You can see this gradient visualized when you toggle "Visualize" (brighter = higher Q-value).
howQLearningLearns.smartFeature1: Difficulty-Adjusted Learning: Easy mazes learn faster (higher α), hard mazes explore more (higher ε decay)
howQLearningLearns.smartFeature2: Reward Shaping: Direction bonus helps agent find goal faster without knowing maze structure
howQLearningLearns.smartFeature3: Demo Mode: Click "Demo" to see pure exploitation (ε=0) - shows what agent truly learned without exploration!

technicalArchitecture.title: Technical Architecture
technicalArchitecture.mazeGeneration: Maze Generation: Recursive backtracker algorithm (depth-first search)
technicalArchitecture.stateSpace: State Space: Discrete grid (row, col) positions
technicalArchitecture.actionSpace: Action Space: 4 discrete actions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT)
technicalArchitecture.backend: Q-Learning Backend: Python (PyScript) with Q-table dictionary storage
technicalArchitecture.rewardShaping: Reward Shaping: Manhattan distance bonus to guide learning
technicalArchitecture.animation: Animation System: Frame-based tweening (60fps) for demo mode smooth movement
technicalArchitecture.visualization: Visualization: Canvas rendering with Q-value heatmap overlay (blue→yellow gradient)
technicalArchitecture.trainingSpeed: Training Speed: ~4 episodes for 50% success on easy mode!

howToUse.title: How to Use
howToUse.step1Desc: Click "Generate" to create a random maze. Try different difficulties!
howToUse.step2Note: Watch the blue agent blink rapidly between cells as it explores!
howToUse.step3Desc: Click "Visualize" to toggle the heatmap overlay
howToUse.step3Note: Blue cells = low Q-value | Yellow cells = high Q-value (closer to goal)
howToUse.step4Desc: Watch Success Rate climb and Epsilon decay as the agent learns
howToUse.step5Desc: Once trained, click "Demo" to see smooth, confident movement
howToUse.step5Note: Agent moves smoothly (tweened) because it's using pure exploitation (ε=0)
howToUse.step6Desc: Try Easy (10×10) vs Insane (30×30) to see how learning adapts!
howToUse.proTip: Pro Tip: Training = agent blinks frantically between spots (exploring). Demo = agent glides smoothly (exploiting learned knowledge)!

whyQLearning.title: Why Q-Learning?
whyQLearning.intro: Q-Learning is the perfect introduction to reinforcement learning because:
whyQLearning.intuitive: Intuitive: Easy to visualize and understand
whyQLearning.modelFree: Model-Free: No knowledge of maze structure needed
whyQLearning.offPolicy: Off-Policy: Learns optimal policy while exploring
whyQLearning.convergence: Guaranteed Convergence: Proven to find optimal solution
whyQLearning.foundation: Foundation for Deep RL: Basis for DQN, Double DQN, etc.

limitations.title: Q-Table Limitations
limitations.intro: Q-tables work great for discrete, small state spaces like mazes. But they don't scale:
limitations.memory: Memory: A 30×30 maze has 900 states × 4 actions = 3,600 Q-values
limitations.continuous: Continuous States: Can't handle pixel inputs or continuous observations
limitations.generalization: Generalization: Each state learned independently, no transfer
limitations.conclusion: That's why complex games like Mario use neural networks (function approximation) instead of Q-tables. Check out the Neuroevolution example to see how!
